messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/d3lc00683b1.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/D3LC00683B

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics with Distance-Based Detection (DMF-DBD) for Semi-Quantitative Nucleic Acid Diagnostics (RT-LAMP detection of SARS-CoV-2 from saliva)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Saliva Sample (lysed, column-extracted and purified viral RNA)
  - Lysis Buffer
  - RT Mastermix (reverse-transcription reagents, converts viral RNA to cDNA)
  - LAMP Mastermix (isothermal amplification reagents for cDNA)
  - Capto(TM) Adhere Agarose Bead Suspension (amplicon clean-up reagent)
  - Wash Buffer
  - SYBR(TM) Safe Intercalating Dye (fluorescent staining reagent for purified LAMP amplicons)

STEPS:
1. Sample lysis: Combine the saliva sample with lysis buffer and incubate at 95 C for 5 min to release viral RNA.
2. Reverse transcription: Mix the lysate with RT mastermix; incubate 15 min at 42 C then 5 min at 65 C to reverse-transcribe viral RNA into cDNA.
3. RT-LAMP amplification: Mix the cDNA with LAMP mastermix and incubate isothermally at 65 C for 30 min to generate LAMP amplicons.
4. Amplicon clean-up: Mix the LAMP product with a suspension of Capto(TM) Adhere agarose beads; incubate 5 min at 25 C, then wash three times with wash buffer to remove unincorporated primers and reduce background fluorescence.
5. Dye staining: Mix the purified, bead-cleaned amplicons with SYBR(TM) Safe intercalating dye.
6. Distance-based detection: Deliver the stained amplicon mixture to the distance-based detection (DBD) paper substrate; measure the resulting fluorescent signal (travel distance/intensity) to semi-quantitatively determine viral load in the sample, then discard the analyzed droplet.

module fluorescence

manifest saliva_sample
manifest lysis_buffer
manifest rt_mastermix
manifest lamp_mastermix
manifest capto_adhere_beads
manifest wash_buffer
manifest sybr_safe_dye

instructions:

sample = dispense 50 units of saliva_sample
lysis = dispense 50 units of lysis_buffer
lysate = mix sample with lysis for 60s
heat lysate at 95c for 5m

rt_mix = dispense 20 units of rt_mastermix
rt_rxn = mix lysate with rt_mix for 30s
heat rt_rxn at 42c for 15m
heat rt_rxn at 65c for 5m

lamp_mix = dispense 30 units of lamp_mastermix
lamp_rxn = mix rt_rxn with lamp_mix for 30s
heat lamp_rxn at 65c for 30m

beads = dispense 20 units of capto_adhere_beads
cleanup = mix lamp_rxn with beads for 60s
heat cleanup at 25c for 5m

repeat 3 times {
    wash = dispense 100 units of wash_buffer
    cleanup = mix cleanup with wash for 30s
}

dye = dispense 10 units of sybr_safe_dye
stained = mix cleanup with dye for 30s

signal = detect fluorescence on stained for 10m

if (signal < 80) {
    dispose stained
}

heat stained at 25c for 1m
dispose stained

ir.content:
main:
	sample1[0] = dispense(saliva_sample)
	lysis1[0] = dispense(lysis_buffer)
	lysate1[0] = mix(sample1[0], lysis1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	heat(lysate1[0]) @ 95.0CELSIUS @ 300.0SECOND
	rt_mix1[0] = dispense(rt_mastermix)
	rt_rxn1[0] = mix(lysate1[0], rt_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(rt_rxn1[0]) @ 42.0CELSIUS @ 900.0SECOND
	heat(rt_rxn1[0]) @ 65.0CELSIUS @ 300.0SECOND
	lamp_mix1[0] = dispense(lamp_mastermix)
	lamp_rxn1[0] = mix(rt_rxn1[0], lamp_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(lamp_rxn1[0]) @ 65.0CELSIUS @ 1800.0SECOND
	beads1[0] = dispense(capto_adhere_beads)
	cleanup1[0] = mix(lamp_rxn1[0], beads1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	heat(cleanup1[0]) @ 25.0CELSIUS @ 300.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_31 = {REPEAT_30,REPEAT_32}
	PHI wash1 = {wash0,wash2}
	PHI cleanup2 = {cleanup1,cleanup3}
	if REPEAT_31[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	wash2[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	cleanup3[0] = mix(cleanup2[0], wash2[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	REPEAT_32[0] = REPEAT_31[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	dye1[0] = dispense(sybr_safe_dye)
	stained1[0] = mix(cleanup2[0], dye1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	signal1[0] = detect(fluorescence, stained1[0]) @ 600.0SECOND
	if signal1[0] < 80	|	true: jump bsbbif_5_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_6_f
bsbbif_5_t:
	dispose(stained1[0])
bsbbif_6_f:
	PHI stained2 = {stained1,stained}
	heat(stained2[0]) @ 25.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	dispose(stained2[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper performs RNA extraction/purification with a physical spin-column prior to DMF loading; BioScript has no solid-phase-extraction primitive, so this is abstracted as a generic lysis mix/heat step rather than a discrete column-based operation.

Detection in the paper is a distance-based readout (fluorescent front travel distance on a paper substrate, imaged by eye or cell-phone camera per Figure S3), not a plate-reader fluorescence intensity value. 'detect fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect module exposed by BioScript's grammar; it stands in for the DBD travel-distance measurement, not a conventional fluorescence intensity reading.

Figure S4C shows a dose-response of normalized travel distance across 0/4/6/8/10 uL wash volumes rather than a fixed integer repeat count; three wash cycles is a reasonable discretization chosen for this translation, not a value stated verbatim in the SI text.

numeric_mismatches.field: DMF cartridge hardware layout (Figure S6A), cell-phone imaging apparatus (Figure S3), qPCR comparison (Table S1)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are hardware-configuration, imaging-instrumentation, or orthogonal validation sub-experiments run alongside the core assay, not part of the lysis-through-detection protocol itself, and fall outside the scope of this translation.
